newsitem.title: USA: Late NYMEX Hub natgas gains more on firm Aug. cash.
newsitem.headline: Late NYMEX Hub natgas gains more on firm Aug. cash.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures continued to edge higher late Wednesday in thin trade, still boosted by reports of firmer August physical prices and forecasts for warmer Midwest and eastern weather this week.
At 1438 EDT, September climbed 4.5 cents to $2.158 per million British thermal units, while October was 3.4 cents higher at $2.15. Most others were steady to up 2.8 cents.

"I don't have a strong opinion, but we do have some warmer weather ahead, so I expect we may trade up a little," said one Texas-based trader, adding he did not expect the new spot-September contract to break out of the recent range.

Despite relatively cool Midwest and East Coast weather this week, traders noted the cash, helped by steady injection demand and some heat in Texas, has stayed unexpectedly firm, setting a more bullish tone during August bidweek this week.
But few expected the bulls to take full control without more significant heat or the threat of a hurricane.
"A hurricane is worth 15 cents, but right now I don't see us breaking out of the range," an East Coast trader said.
Below-normal temperatures are blanketing the East and Midwest this week, but normal to slightly above-normal weather was forecast for the weekend.

Chart traders said September also seemed to be stuck in a range, with support at $2.08 and then at last week's low of $2.045. Resistance was pegged first at the triple top at $2.16 and then at recent $2.20 high.

In the cash Wednesday, August Gulf Coast gas firmed a few cents to the mid-to-high teens. August Midcon was up a couple of cents to the $2.07-2.10 area. New York city gate gas for next month was little changed in the low-$2.40s.
A Reuter poll of industry players showed most expected a weekly AGA stock build tonight in the 75-85 bcf range versus a gain last year of 81 bcf.
NYMEX said 9,112 contracts traded at 1140 EDT.

On the KCBT, August, which expires later today, was still up 3.7 cents at $2.155, while deferreds remained steady to three cents higher. The September East/West spread widened by 1.5 cents to 9.8 cents (NYMEX premium).
